operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: the order's single operative sentence amends sec. 403 of EO 10161 by redesignating para. (b) as (c) and inserting a new para. (b) providing up to two labor and two industry alternate members of the Wage Stabilization Board (held FR text 17 FR 7995, offsets 794-2450). First end: EO 10480 sec. 607(11), 1953-08-14, which names EO 10390 by number and date; EO 10480 sec. 607(1) also supersedes the parent EO 10161 in the same sentence. The order has no term, sunset or condition of its own. Disclosed earlier candidates (not ends under the 2026-10-21 unnamed-instruments ruling, because none names EO 10390): (a) EO 10434 of 1953-02-06 (held, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10434.txt, para. 1 at offset 1715) suspends 'All regulations and orders issued pursuant to the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, stabilizing wages, salaries, and other compensation'; it does not name EO 10390 or EO 10161 and does not abolish the Board or its alternate-member paragraph; (b) EO 10467 of 1953-06-30 sec. 1 (held, EO_10467.txt offsets 3783-4200) keeps DPA delegation orders in force only 'with respect to such of the said functions as are continued by the Defense Production Act Amendments of 1953'; if those Amendments did not continue Title IV wage stabilization, the alternate-member paragraph may have been displaced from 1953-06-30 or the Title IV expiry; the Amendments are not held (FETCH_QUEUE line 317 already requests them); EO 10467 does not name EO 10390. Neither is an end under the ruling; both are disclosed for the human reviewer. No later amendment of the inserted para. 403(b) was found: EO 10433 sec. 2 (1953-02-04) rewrites only sec. 401(a) of EO 10161. No later event is attached.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Defense Production Act of 1950, 
as amended (50 U. S. C. App. 2061 et 
seq.), and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered that section 403 of 
Executive Order No. 10161 of September 
9, 1950 (15 P. R. 6105), as amended, be, 
and it is hereby, further amended by 
redesignating paragraph (b) thereof as 
paragraph (c) and by inserting im­
mediately after paragraph (a) thereof 
the following new paragraph:
“(b) In addition to the members of 
the Wage Stabilization Board provided 
for in section 403 (a) of this order, the 
Board shall have not more than two 
alternate members who shall be repre­
sentative of labor and not more than 
two alternate members who shall be 
representative of business and industry. 
Alternate members shall be appointed 
by the President, by and with the advice 
and consent of the Senate, at such times 
as he may deem necessary. Any alter­
nate member shall participate as a mem­
ber of the Board only in lieu of a member 
appointed under section 403 (a) of this 
order who is not participating, and only 
when called upon by the Chairman of the 
Wage Stabilization Board to so partici­
pate, and when so participating each 
alternate member shall have the same 
status and functions as a member ap­
pointed under the said section 403 (a). 
The designation by the Chairman of the 
Board of alternate members to partici­
pate as members of the Board shall be 
so ordered as to preserve the equal rep- ' 
resentation required by the provisions of 
section 403 (a) hereof and of section 
403 (b) of the Defense Production Act 
of 1950, as amended.”
x  Harry S. T ruman

research_rationale: EO 10390 (signed 1952-08-30, 17 FR 7995, FR issue of 1952-09-04), read in full from the held official FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10390.txt, offsets 794-2450): one sentence amending sec. 403 of EO 10161 to add alternate members of the Wage Stabilization Board. The dossier's single clause covers the whole operative text to the signature. Ending: EO 10480 (signed 1953-08-14, 18 FR 4939-4944) sec. 607 supersedes or revokes '(11) Executive Order No. 10390 of August 30, 1952 (17 F. R. 7995)' (held FR text EO_10480.txt offsets 39234-39302) and its parent EO 10161 (item (1)); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1953-08-14. The ACT record cited is APP-sourced; its wording matches the held FR text except the APP year misprint '1962'. D6: dossier chain (only EO 10480), ACT provisions (three EO 10480 records, same sec. 607), draft later-event proposals (EO 10480 only), OFR catalog note 'Superseded by: EO 10480, August 14, 1953', by-number scan of the held FR texts, and the held EO 10161-related orders of 1952-1953 (EO 10433, 10434, 10461, 10467). Earlier candidates disclosed, not ends (unnamed-instruments ruling 2026-10-21): EO 10434 (1953-02-06, wage-control suspension, does not touch the alternate-member paragraph) and EO 10467 sec. 1 with the unheld Defense Production Act Amendments of 1953 (possible statutory displacement of Title IV functions from mid-1953; FETCH_QUEUE line 317). The 2026-10-20 Lambertini i04 review rejected an earlier claim for this order because that claim called the EO 10480 date an upper bound while listing no gap; under the 2026-10-21 ruling the end is the naming instrument (EO 10480) and the statutory lead is a disclosed candidate only. Conflicts: none listed. Savings: transferred_or_accrued under EO 10480 sec. 606. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10480 sec. 606 (held official FR text EO_10480.txt offsets 37981-38457; the cited evidence is the same sentence in the APP transcription): 'All orders, regulations, rulings, certificates, directives and other actions relating to any function affected by this order shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended or revoked under proper authority, and nothing in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything heretofore done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended.' Actions already taken under EO 10161 sec. 403(b) as inserted by EO 10390 (appointments of alternate members, their participation) keep their validity; the alternate-member rule itself is not re-enacted by EO 10480, and EO 10480 sec. 605 continues the Economic Stabilization Agency only to October 31, 1953 for winding up. EO 10390 itself has no savings wording. Bounded search: EO 10390 and EO 10480 read in full in the held FR texts; by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts for '10390' (hits: EO 10480 sec. 607(11) and its FR contents list; EO 10481 and 10482, which share the FR pages of EO 10480; an unrelated tariff number in EO 14257).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: the order's single operative sentence extends 'until June 20, 1961, the time within which the emergency board created by Executive Order No. 10919 of February 17, 1961 ... shall report its findings to the President' (held FR text 26 FR 2331, offsets 837-1380). This is a report deadline, which is never an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C; the 'until' date governs the time to report, not the life of the order). The report was made on 1961-06-20 (attached as a spent-fact later event, functionally spent on 1961-06-20). First end: EO 12553 row 10926, 1986-02-25 on signing. No other held order names EO 10926 (by-number scan of 6,652 held FR texts: only EO 12553 and EO 10926 itself; the other '10926' hits are FR page numbers in 1942 contents lists of EO 9285/9286/9289). No further extension of PEB 135's time was found: the report itself (offsets 14293-14332 region) recites only the EO 10926 extension 'until June 20, 1961'.

later_events.mechanism: spent fact, not an end (owner report-deadline ruling 2026-10-21, option C): Emergency Board No. 135 made its report to the President on 1961-06-20, the last day of the time EO 10926 allowed. Held NMB copy of the report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10926_Actual_report_date_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10919_time_extended_by_EO_109_c9777d82c1.txt, PEB-135-Report.pdf sha256 b1d3ce3b...): cover 'WASHINGTON, D.C. / JUNE 20, 1961 / (No. 135)' (offsets 1207-1220) and 'LETTER OF TRANSMITTAL' (1259-1280) in which the Board 'has the honor to submit herewith its report' (1731-1774); the transmittal date line is OCR-damaged ('June ~0~ 1961'), so the date rests on the cover. From this date the extension granted by EO 10926 was functionally spent (functionally spent on 1961-06-20). The RLA sec. 10 standstill of 30 days after the report (to 1961-07-20) is imposed by EO 10919 and the statute, not by EO 10926, which contains no standstill clause; it is recorded here only as information. The cited evidence span is the report's cover heading; the date line follows it at the offsets given.

research_rationale: EO 10926 (signed 1961-03-18, 26 FR 2331, FR issue of 1961-03-21), read in full from the held official FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10926.txt, offsets 837-1380): one sentence extending until June 20, 1961 the time for Emergency Board No. 135 (created by EO 10919 of 1961-02-17, Pan American World Airways / Flight Engineers) to report. The dossier's single clause is the whole operative text. Owner report-deadline ruling (2026-10-21, option C) applied: the deadline and the report are spent facts, not ends. The board reported on 1961-06-20 (held NMB report copy, cover date at offsets 1207-1220 of jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10926_Actual_report_date_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10919_time_extended_by_EO_109_c9777d82c1.txt), recorded as a later event with the note 'functionally spent on 1961-06-20'.
